Use `File` and `Form` together as parameters in the same path operation. Use `File` and `Form` together when you need to receive data and files in the same request.[1]

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, Form, UploadFile

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/files/")
async def create_file(
    title: Annotated[str, Form()],
    attachment: Annotated[UploadFile, File()],
):
    return {"title": title, "filename": attachment.filename}
```

The files and form fields will be uploaded as form data and you will receive the files and form fields.[2] You can declare some of the files as `bytes` and some as `UploadFile`.[2] If you declare a file as `bytes`, the whole contents will be stored in memory. This will work well for small files.[5]

**Things to know:**

- **Install `python-multipart` first.** To receive uploaded files and/or form data, first install `python-multipart`[2], for example with `uv add python-multipart`.
- **You can't mix in JSON body fields.** You can declare multiple `File` and `Form` parameters in a *path operation*, but you can't also declare `Body` fields that you expect to receive as JSON, as the request will have the body encoded using `multipart/form-data` instead of `application/json`.[2] This is not a limitation of **FastAPI**, it's part of the HTTP protocol.[2]
- **You can group form fields in a model.** You can also combine a form model with file parameters[4]:

```python
class Profile(BaseModel):
    name: str


@app.post("/profiles/")
async def create_profile(profile: Annotated[Profile, Form()], avatar: UploadFile):
    return {"profile": profile, "filename": avatar.filename}
```
